lesson_title: VAT, UIF, Tariffs and Exchange Rates: the Numbers Running Your Wallet
hook_text: The till says R414. The shop only keeps R360. Who pocketed the other R54 — and why does taking 15% off give the WRONG answer?
clip_script: R360 kettle. Add fifteen percent VAT — R54 — and the till rings R414. Simple. Now reverse it: the slip says R414, what was the price before tax? Everyone knocks fifteen percent off. Everyone is wrong. Fifteen percent of 414 is 62,10 — too big, because 414 is already the taxed number. The slip is 115 percent of the truth, so DIVIDE by 1,15: R360, exactly. Next, the payslip. UIF: one percent of gross. Slide the comma — R9 200 becomes R92. And the part nobody sees: the boss pays another R92 straight to the fund. The fund banks R184; the payslip admits to R92. Now the phone shop. Deal P: R120 a month plus 60 cents a minute. Deal Q: no fee, R1,40 a minute. Talk 100 minutes? Q wins, R140 to R180. Talk 250? P wins, R270 to R350. They swap at exactly 150 minutes. Fixed fee for the big talker, pay-as-you-go for the quiet one. Direction and rate — that is your whole wallet.
visual_style: A till slip unrolling with the VAT line glowing; a payslip splitting into two R92 coins, one on the slip and one sliding in from the employer's side; two phone-deal cost lines racing up a graph and crossing at 150 minutes.
mood: Sharp, consumer-savvy, slightly conspiratorial — the friend who checks the slip before leaving the till.
pacing: Quick on the VAT trap, a beat of surprise on the hidden R92, accelerating through the phone-deal race to the break-even point.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and out-calculate every till, payslip and phone deal.
